title: GPU capacity escape-hatch, predictive warmup experiments, and soft-failover playbook
creator: Sara Kim
description: Summary: After the recent GPU exhaustion incident where request queues built up and throttling caused cascading customer errors, we need a short-term escape hatch and a set of medium-term experiments to reduce likelihood and blast radius of future events. This ticket captures: (1) a fast, testable "escape hatch" that can be toggled during spikes to reroute noncritical traffic to a degraded but safe execution path; (2) predictive warmup/autoscale experiments that prime GPU pools based on burst-derivative signals rather than simple rate thresholds; and (3) soft-failover policies for tenant-facing degradations (serve CPU-quantized models, cached responses, or reject with friendly 429 + retry-after). The goal is to reduce queue amplification, shorten time-to-recovery, and make operational remediation less manual.
background: On 2026-02-10 we observed a 3x sustained incoming QPS delta in a subset of tenants which caused GPU pools to hit allocation limits and long tail queue growth. Existing autoscaler reacted too late due to conservative ramp limits and pooling hysteresis. Prefill and KV cache pollution amplified per-tenant slot occupation; admission controls degraded fairness. Oncall mitigations included manual emergency scaling and tenant throttles which are brittle and high-friction.
success_criteria: Median queue length during simulated burst reduced by >=50% compared to baseline
P95 latency for critical tenants maintained within SLO under modeled bursts
Automated escape-hatch activation reduces customer error rate within 30s in blue-green canary tests
Rollback plan validated for escape-hatch without cross-pool side effects
work_items: Implement toggleable escape-hatch flow in gateway: route lower-priority requests to degraded path (cpu-quantized model / cached response) (owner: Marcus)
Add fast signal: compute burst-derivative (dQPS/dt) and publish to autoscaler queue (owner: Elena)
Autoscaler experiments: decrease scale-up cooldown, add graded prewarm for predicted bursts (owner: Ops team)
Tenant soft-quotas: enforce temporary per-tenant cap + graceful 426/429 with Retry-After + guidance (owner: PM)
KV cache lockdown mode during emergency to avoid pollution (owner: Runtime)
Integration tests and chaos scenarios in staging for escape-hatch + autoscale (owner: SRE)
Dashboard panels and alerting for derivative signal and escape-hatch activations (owner: Observability)
Run tabletop + oncall playbook update and schedule runbook drill (owner: Incident Commander)
Post-experiment cost analysis and rollout recommendation (owner: Finance Eng)
Write evaluation doc with results, include PRs and playbook snippets (owner: Sara)
implementation_notes: Escape-hatch design: a simple policy flag in routing layer that matches requests by priority label and tenant. When enabled, the router will: 1) attempt to serve from local prefix cache; 2) if miss and request priority is low, forward to CPU-quantized fallback model with bounded token limit; 3) if fallback unavailable, return structured 429 with Retry-After and an inline hint to client to reduce token budget. This flow must preserve tenant isolation and not starve critical traffic. Autoscaler experiment: evaluate two heuristics in parallel for 2 weeks: (A) derivative-based proactive prewarm (scale when dQPS/dt > threshold), and (B) exponential moving-average with short half-life + aggressive burst capacity. Telemetry: emit events when escape-hatch routes >5% of traffic and when derivative triggers scale-up. Add guardrails to prevent oscillation (min up-time 60s, cool-down 90s).
risks: Escape-hatch may increase cost if too permissive (running extra CPU fallbacks)
Incorrect derivative thresholds could over-trigger or miss bursts
KV lockdown may increase miss rate and upstream latency temporarily
Tenant soft-quotas risk customer complaints if messaging is not clear
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (48h): Implement escape-hatch behind feature flag in staging and run synthetic spike tests. Phase 1 (1 week): Canary to 2 internal tenants with feature on for non-critical routes. Phase 2 (2 weeks): Run autoscaler experiments in parallel clusters with A/B metric collection. Phase 3: If successful, promote to clusters with conservative rollout schedule and update runbook for oncall activation criteria.
acceptance_criteria: All automated canary checks pass (no cross-pool latency regression >15%), escape-hatch toggles within 30s from Console toggle, derivative-based prewarm shows >=30% earlier scale events on synthetic bursts without increased oscillation.
